name: WebAssembly
version_context: WebAssembly core specification repository commit b0ec1f3f449525c217dbff3f1dfab435a756ea92
summary: A typed portable instruction format and abstract machine with validation, module-scoped definitions, store-owned runtime instances, structured control, and explicit embedder boundaries.

features.name: Typed module validation
features.description: The WebAssembly core specification defines value, instruction, module, and matching rules that validate modules before execution. Validation checks that instruction sequences and module components satisfy their declared types and limits.
benefits: Rejects malformed or ill-typed modules before execution
Creates a portable contract between producers and embedders
costs: The type and validation rules constrain expressiveness at the module boundary
Implementations must maintain validation and execution agreement

features.name: Structured stack-machine execution
features.description: WebAssembly execution uses an interleaved stack containing values and control frames such as labels, call frames, and exception handlers. Structured control instructions reduce through these frames, and traps represent abrupt termination.
benefits: Provides a compact, portable execution semantics
Makes control-flow and activation boundaries explicit in the abstract machine
costs: Stack and control-frame invariants must be preserved by implementations
The abstract machine leaves optimization and host scheduling to implementations

features.name: Store-owned module instances
features.description: The specification models global runtime state in a store containing instances of functions, tables, memories, globals, and other entities. A module instance collects runtime representations of imported, defined, and exported entities, while host functions remain an embedder-defined boundary.
benefits: Separates static module indices from dynamic runtime addresses
Defines a precise object boundary for instantiation and embedding
costs: Embedding requires explicit mapping of imports, exports, and host behavior
Store and instance state add lifecycle and resource-management obligations

features.name: Bounded linear memory
features.description: A WebAssembly memory instance is a typed sequence of bytes whose length is a multiple of the 64 KiB page size and cannot exceed its declared maximum. Memory mutation occurs through instructions, data segments, or permitted embedder actions.
benefits: Gives modules a portable byte-addressable resource with explicit growth limits
Makes memory size and mutation part of the module contract
costs: Fixed page and maximum-size rules constrain resource layout
The embedder must account for growth failures and host-side access policy

mathematical_views.question: When does a module's instruction sequence satisfy the types, limits, and component contracts required for instantiation?
assumptions: Instruction sequences and module components are related by the specification's typing and matching judgments
Validation precedes execution and does not model implementation-specific compilation
The view abstracts host policy beyond the import and export contract

mathematical_views.question: How do store instances, module frames, control labels, and operand values evolve during execution?
assumptions: A configuration consists of a store, current frame, and remaining instruction sequence
Administrative labels, frames, handlers, and traps are transitions of the abstract machine
The view does not assert that an implementation uses a literal operand stack

mathematical_views.question: Which properties of a WebAssembly execution remain specification invariants, and which are supplied by the embedder?
assumptions: Module validation and store invariants are specification-level properties
Host function behavior and host addresses are external inputs to the abstract machine
The hypothesis requires comparison across concrete embedders to determine practical isolation guarantees

benefits: Portable pre-execution type and limit checks
costs: Validation rules constrain module expressiveness and implementation freedom

benefits: Explicit portable control and activation semantics
costs: Control-frame invariants add implementation and reasoning work

benefits: Clear runtime ownership and import/export boundary
costs: Instantiation and host integration require lifecycle coordination
Page, growth, and maximum-size constraints shape resource design
